chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who comes to the mosque while they are in prayer, and the Imam has already led him by one rak'ah or more. The Imam falls ill, so he takes his hand, and he happens to be the closest of the people to him, so he appoints him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He completes the prayer of the people, then sits until they finish the Tashahhud, and he gestures to them with his hand to the right and left. Thus, his gesture to them with his hand is the Taslim (greeting), and the completion of their prayer, and he completes whatever was missed by him or remains upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a latecomer who leads the congregation when the Imam falls ill?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the procedure for a latecomer (*muqtadi*) who becomes the acting Imam when the primary Imam is incapacitated, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of congregational prayer (*Jama'ah*). It clarifies that the latecomer completes the congregation's prayer by performing the final Taslim, while separately fulfilling his own missed or remaining rak'ahs, ensuring both the communal and individual obligations are met correctly. This ruling underscores the scholarly principle that the validity of the congregation's prayer is preserved even if the leadership transitions mid-prayer due to necessity.
